title: Four phases make a cabin no polar bear can open, in 14 weeks
subtitle: Standard two-room cabin on Arctic coastal permafrost, 2026 build programme

items.heading: Weeks 1-3
items.label: Survey and anchor
details: Map every den within 5 km, and keep clear of whale bones
Drive 24 steel piles into the permafrost, no concrete
Lift the floor 1.8 m above a standing bear's reach
Fence the site in bear wire
Ship the crane before sea ice
Log the wind and the drifts
Survey signed off by week 3, before the first snow

items.heading: Weeks 4-7
items.label: Armour the shell
details: Spruce walls 30 cm thick
Steel mesh under the cladding on every side, roof included
No bins, bird feeders or fish sheds within 50 m of the walls
Roof pitched at 45°
Vents set above 3 m
Insulated to minus 45°C, so the stove can stay small
Seams glued, so there is no smell of dinner outside

items.heading: Weeks 8-11
items.label: Doors and windows
details: Doors open inwards only
Window bars rated to hold 900 kg of inquisitive bear
Shutters close from inside in under 20 seconds flat
No outside door handles
Bear-rated glass, 4 cm thick, in every window frame
Porch kept bare: bears open anything resembling a box
Dog flap strictly forbidden

items.heading: Weeks 12-14
items.label: Test and hand over
details: Fortnight-long trial using a decoy that smells of sardines
Zero break-ins in 31 trial cabins built since 2022
Owner drills: shutters, flares and the emergency radio
Keys and a flare gun
Bear-proof rating signed off
Welcome hamper, no fish inside
Free check-up each spring for the first five years

bar: Bears pull but rarely push, so inward doors kept 31 trial cabins at zero break-ins.

title: Heavier pumpkins pull bigger crowds, and the crowds pay for next year's heavier pumpkins
subtitle: League growth loop, 2023 to 2026 seasons

items.label: Heavier pumpkins
items.text: The record reaches 1,140 kg

items.label: Bigger crowds
items.text: 14,000 at the weigh-off

items.label: Richer prize pot
items.text: Gate money lifts it to £60,000

items.label: Better seed
items.text: Winners' seeds sold at auction

items.label: Warmer greenhouses
items.text: Prize money buys heated tunnels

points.text: Every 100 kg added to the record brings about 2,000 more spectators, and this year's champion weighed in at 1,140 kg.
Gate money pays 60% of the £60,000 prize pot, and a pumpkin-soup stall and a tractor raffle cover the rest.
Winners' seeds fetch up to £800 each at the spring auction, and one champion's seed grew a third of this year's finalists.
A wet August breaks the loop: rot cost three finalists their pumpkins in 2025, and the weigh-off crowd fell by a fifth.

title: A six-week export permit, not the lab, sets the pace from desert to pendant
subtitle: Supply chain for one meteorite, find to finished jewellery, 2026

nodes.label: Desert hunt
nodes.text: Bought from hunters in Morocco and Chile

nodes.label: Authenticity lab
nodes.text: Nickel and iron assay, takes three weeks

nodes.label: Export permit
nodes.text: Customs and heritage papers, six weeks

nodes.label: Slicing
nodes.text: Diamond saw, 1 mm slices, one week

nodes.label: Setting
nodes.text: Silver bezels set by hand, two weeks

nodes.label: Boutique
nodes.text: Sold in a velvet crater box, with a certificate

points.text: The lab and the permit run side by side; the permit's six weeks, not the lab's three, set the pace.
From find to boutique takes nine weeks: six for the permit, one at the saw and two at the bench.
Only 1 in 4 rocks the hunters send passes the nickel test; the other three are slag or gravel.
Slicing turns 40% of each rock into dust, so a 1 kg find makes about 60 pendants, not the 100 hoped for.

points.text: Browsing is healthy: 62 of every 100 visitors open a treehouse page, well above the travel-site norm of 45.
Half of them leave at the calendar, because weekend nights sell out eight weeks ahead.
The waiver page loses 22 of the 31 who picked dates; it opens with a diagram of the drop.
Payment is the smallest leak: 6 of the 9 who sign the waiver then go on to pay.
Move the waiver after payment as one checkbox and bookings could rise from 6 to about 15 in 100.

title: Every £9,500 shower rests on £7,000 of cost, and the forecast sets the margin
subtitle: Average cost per seeded storm, FY26, 212 storms flown
highlight: over a third of the cost

layers.label: Rain guarantee
layers.text: £1,200 per storm in refunds, paid whenever the sky stays stubbornly dry for 48 hours after seeding

layers.label: Seeding flights
layers.text: £2,600 per storm for aircraft, pilots and fuel, paid in full whether the cloud cooperates or not

layers.label: Flares and chemistry
layers.text: £600 per storm for silver iodide flares, two per cloud, plus the occasional dud that only fizzles

layers.label: Permits and ground crew
layers.text: £800 per storm for airspace permits, landowner consents and the crew who watch the windsock

layers.label: Forecast and radar desk
layers.text: £1,800 per storm for the meteorologists and radar that decide which clouds are worth chasing

points.text: Better forecasts pick clouds that actually rain: 78% of flights did in FY26, up from 61%. Refunds fell from £2,100 to £1,200 a storm, so cost is now £7,000 against a £9,500 price.
Aircraft, pilots and fuel are over a third of the cost, and a flight costs the same whether or not the cloud cooperates. Choosing the right cloud beats flying cheaper.
The flares cost £600 a storm. Clients ask about them more than anything else, and they move the margin least.

source: Source: Synthetic demonstration • no real company data; the duty forecaster's soggy clipboard

title: The 1999 capsules are one step from reopening, 409 of 412 intact
subtitle: Vault B, the batch of 412 capsules sealed in December 1999, at October 2026

items.label: Intake
items.detail: 412 capsules logged, weighed and X-rayed for anything that might rot, leak or hatch before 2027

items.label: Seal
items.detail: Argon-filled steel tubes, each welded shut and stamped with the date its owner chose to open it

items.label: Store
items.detail: Kept at 12°C and 35% humidity, 40 metres down in a former salt mine, checked by torch every month

items.label: Inspect
items.detail: Every capsule weighed again: 409 unchanged, and three re-sealed after slow leaks of argon

items.label: Reopen
items.detail: Owners, or their grandchildren, invited to a ceremony with cake, speeches and a hacksaw each

points.text: 409 capsules passed the weigh-in with no loss of argon, including the one that rattles in a worrying way
Three leaky capsules, all welded on one afternoon in 1999, were re-sealed and checked twice in September
Owners traced: 377 of 412 so far, with the last 35 being found through old school registers by March 2027
Hacksaws sharpened, a marquee booked and a very large cake ordered for the reopening ceremony next June
